title: Bix Beiderbecke, and rhythm as Black heritage versus modern pop singers
summary: Greer says Bix was a friend and was overrated, then rants about current pop stars and Black music heritage; the church question is cut off.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: They immortalize this guy. You couldn't put Bix Beiderbecke on a bandstand if you had a derrick and lift him up there. When them cats, when all them trumpet players got to playing, what can you do. He stopped -- tear him up (unintelligible) He was a good friend of mine, Bix was, because everytime we went to Davenport, I would go out to see his people. I hear 'em talk about this guy and that guy, it's a living joke man. It's a masquerade, because you don't have to go hunting for them. You could walk by a little old dive, and hear the damndest music and singing you ever heard in your life. You know what I'm talking about.

These cats -- they don't do nothing. You get one of those chicks, with the $3.00 hair, get a $3.00 guitar and she go out and sing the water's wet, the wind is blowing and right away I see a guy like Merv Griffin, Mike Douglas and

them guys, how many gold records you got. I got 15, 20. They must be giving them away like handbills. They couldn't have made Major Bowes' Amateur Hour. They don't know when the music start, by the colored. They ain't saying nothing. It was put up or shut up. You either had it or you didn't have it. If you didn't have it, you just move aside.

Wasn't no in between, because these people know no talent, as I said, music is our heritage, dancing. Music and dancing, ain't picking no cotton, our heritage. Rhythm is our heritage. You understand what I mean, all them people singing. They caught it from Negro churches. They don't know nothing about that.
They kill me when they talk about man, I'm singing some soul. SHIT.
Tell me this, what kind of church background did you have? What kind of church did you go to when you were growing up in Long Branch?
It's a wonder Jo Jones didn't tell you about it.
